ticks.claim: No zero of zeta lies off the critical line by way of a Robin (divisor-sum) counterexample at n <= 1,000,000: the sieve finds none in (5040, 1,000,000] (closest approach n=10,080, sigma/(e^gamma n lnln n) = 0.985819 < 1). RH cannot fail by this route below 1,000,000 — a second, independent tool narrowing the window, by elimination.

[by elimination] The Riemann stick is charted by what RH is NOT. Directly: the two independent zero counts agree to height 1e7, so NO zero lies off the line below it. Through the divisor sum (Robin): no counterexample to n=1,000,000. A counterexample to RH, if one exists, must therefore evade every eliminated region at once — the surviving window is where RH remains untested, and each tool narrows it.
